title: A definite integral
steps: The integrand $3x^2 + 2x$ is a polynomial, so it is continuous on $[0, 1]$ and the definite integral exists.
An antiderivative is $F(x) = x^3 + x^2$, because the power rule gives $F'(x) = 3x^2 + 2x$.
By the fundamental theorem of calculus, $\int_0^1 (3x^2 + 2x)\, dx = F(1) - F(0)$.
